severity: real_data_correctness_bug, project-wide scope checked, actual blast radius limited to one not-yet-attested candidate
context: Batch 3's real dry run (workflow run https://github.com/Fahad9101/NRE/actions/runs/36979299010, commit 6deba57) reported a genuine missing_sessions gap for love-step3-2024-12-12: ['2025-01-09']. This is the first missing-session finding anywhere in this project's real history -- every other candidate across M1, M2 step 2, and M2 step 3 batches 1-2 has always shown an empty missing_sessions list.
root_cause: January 9, 2025 was a real, full closure of both NYSE and Nasdaq equities markets, observing the National Day of Mourning for former President Jimmy Carter (died 2024-12-29) -- confirmed via multiple independent real sources (NYSE's and Nasdaq's own announcements, contemporaneous financial press: Fox Business, Nasdaq's own press release, and others). This closure is real, not an Alpaca data gap and not a missing-bar artifact. nre/calendar-2025.json did not list it as a holiday because that file was built (2026-09-28) by reading the official NYSE/ICE 2025 yearly trading calendar PDF directly -- a static document published well before Carter's death, which could not have anticipated a one-time closure announced in response to it. This is not a research error in how the file was originally built; it is a real gap between a static published calendar and a later real-world special announcement.
scope_check: Before fixing anything, checked every already-built event file in this project for a 20-session reaction window spanning 2025-01-09: m1-events.json (0 affected), config/m2-step2-events.json (0 affected), config/m2-combined-events.json (0 affected), config/m2-step3-events.json (1 affected: love-step3-2024-12-12, not yet attested). No already-accepted milestone's own computed labels are affected by this gap.
fix_applied: nre/calendar-2025.json: added '2025-01-09' to holidays, with an amendment_2026_10_02 field explaining why (keeps the original review_note intact rather than overwriting it, same discipline as this project's own calendar-2024.json review_note style). config/m2-step3-merged-calendar.json: regenerated from the corrected nre/calendar-2024.json + nre/calendar-2025.json using nre.depth_cohort.merged_calendar_spec() directly (the project's own real merge function), not hand-edited.
deliberately_not_touched: config/m2-step2-merged-calendar.json carries the same latent gap (2025-01-09 absent) and M1's nre/calendar-2026.json is a different year entirely and was never in scope -- neither is touched, because (a) the scope check above confirms zero real M1 or M2-step2 events are affected by this specific date, and (b) both milestones are already formally accepted, with their own acceptance declarations having hashed and pinned specific file states; editing either file would change a hash that is part of an already-closed record for no actual change in computed output. If a future milestone (M2 step 3 batches 4-6, or any later work) ever adds a candidate whose own window spans 2025-01-09 using the step-2 calendar file specifically, re-visit this decision then.
effect_on_love_step3_2024_12_12: Its own published_at/cutoff/timestamp_evidence are unaffected (those describe the real disclosure moment, not calendar mechanics). Only the computed reaction-session labeling changes: the 20th reaction session shifts from the (wrong) 2025-01-10 to the (correct) 2025-01-13, since 2025-01-09 is no longer miscounted as a tradeable session. This candidate had not yet been attested when the gap was found, so no already-attested result needed correction -- the fix landed before this candidate's first real attested run.
verification: validate_spec() passes on all 30 current step-3 events with the corrected calendar; full test suite green (484 tests, same count as before -- no test anywhere in this project hardcoded the old, incorrect assumption that 2025-01-09 was a trading day).
